frequency_question: How often do states with high will and foreign partner backing successfully establish domestic production lines for advanced precision munitions within a 2-3 year window?
membership_rule: Includes wartime state programs to domesticate advanced missile or precision-guided munition manufacturing with external technical transfer. Excludes peacetime domestic development programs and simple assembly of unguided standard ammunition.

cases.name: Soviet wartime relocation and setup of Ilyushin/Yakovlev and munitions factories
UK wartime emergency production scaling of advanced radar and specialized ordnance
Taiwan domestic production of Hsiung Feng missiles with foreign technological roots
South Korea rapid indigenous defense acquisition and co-production scaling
Ukraine domestic Soviet-legacy missile derivative adaptations (e.g., Neptune development)
Ukraine wartime domestic UAV scaling initiatives

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named cases covering major wartime and acute-threat domestic advanced weapons manufacturing setups.
known_gaps: Extremely high-tech cruise missile co-production under active bombardment has a very sparse direct sample size, forcing reliance on broader wartime advanced munitions domestic setups.
validity_reason: Base rate reflects fundamental dynamics of wartime industrial mobilization under extreme necessity, which remain stable across decades.
